title: The component you just made is the one you can see on the shelf
goal: With a handful of components saved, the shelf shows the first two rows and the rest are behind its own little scroll. Making a new component opens the shelf, but the tile you just made can be sitting below that inner fold, so the shelf is on screen and your work is not. The shelf should be showing the tile you just made.
notes: Follow-on from when-the-library-opens-on-its-own-you-can-see-it, which scrolls the DOCK to the Library section. The shelf itself is a second ScrollView inside LibraryPanel.tiles (Sources/Photonz/LibraryPanel.swift), bounded by inspector.libraryHeight, so it needs its own ScrollViewReader keyed on the entry id. DockReveal (PhotonzCore) already has the pure math for deciding whether anything needs to move. Ordering note: componentEntries lists the document own mains first (layer-stack order) then untaken starters, so a new main is not necessarily first.
acceptance: With enough components to fill more than two rows, making a new one leaves its tile visible inside the shelf without scrolling by hand
A shelf whose new tile is already visible does not scroll
A picture shows the new tile on screen with at least seven components in the document
